title: When is synchronized state fit for a decision?
description: Choose an observation, reconciliation policy, and intended use. The same twin state can be acceptable for a dashboard and unsafe for closed-loop control.

useCases.label: Operator monitoring
useCases.detail: A human reads current condition with a five-second freshness contract.

useCases.label: Fault diagnosis
useCases.detail: A rule explains a transition and requires continuous event history.

useCases.label: Closed-loop control
useCases.detail: A command depends on fresh state and a model validated for this control use.

policies.label: Latest arrival wins
policies.detail: Apply each message when it reaches the consumer, regardless of source sequence.

policies.label: Monotonic source sequence
policies.detail: Reject replayed state and record gaps instead of pretending history is complete.

scenarios.label: Fresh, in-order sample
scenarios.detail: Observation 42 follows the twin's current sequence 41.

arrival-order.reason: The arriving observation replaces the previous value.

scenarios.label: Delayed replay arrives late
scenarios.detail: An old sequence 39 arrives after the twin reached sequence 41.

arrival-order.reason: Arrival order mistakes an old replay for current state.

source-sequence.reason: Sequence 39 is rejected because the twin already holds sequence 41.

scenarios.label: Fresh sample with a gap
scenarios.detail: Sequence 46 arrives while observations 42 through 45 are missing.

arrival-order.reason: The current value advances, but the policy does not explain the missing transition.

source-sequence.reason: The twin advances and explicitly marks sequences 42–45 for backfill.
